title: Instantiate the abstract discrete Carleson theorem to prove finitary Carleson (Proposition 2.0.1)
intent: Reduce the headline Proposition 2.0.1 (finitary Carleson) to the already-proved abstract theorem discrete_carleson, by instantiating the abstract GridStructure/TileStructure typeclasses at the concrete constructions grid_existence and tile_existence, then rewriting the abstract carlesonSum into the concrete per-scale tile sum with tile_sum_operator.

parent.name: finitary_carleson
parent.statement: theorem finitary_carleson : ∃ G', MeasurableSet G' ∧ 2 * volume G' ≤ volume G ∧ ∀ f : X → ℂ, Measurable f → (∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ F.indicator 1 x) → ∫⁻ x in G \ G', ‖∑ s ∈ Icc (σ₁ x) (σ₂ x), ∫ y, Ks s x y * f y * exp (I * Q x y)‖ₑ ≤ C2_0_1 a nnq * (volume G) ^ (1 - q⁻¹) * (volume F) ^ q⁻¹

children.name: discrete_carleson
children.statement: theorem discrete_carleson : ∃ G', MeasurableSet G' ∧ 2 * volume G' ≤ volume G ∧ ∀ f : X → ℂ, Measurable f → (∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ F.indicator 1 x) → ∫⁻ x in G \ G', ‖carlesonSum univ f x‖ₑ ≤ C2_0_2 a nnq * volume G ^ (1 - q⁻¹) * volume F ^ q⁻¹
children.closed_by: a calc chain whose steps are closed by exceptional_set (l.47), forest_union and forest_complement (l.61), and le_C2_0_2 (l.66)

children.closed_by: each GridStructure field constructed from 𝓓, I3_prop_1, I3_prop_3_1, I3_prop_3_2, cover_by_cubes, dyadic_property, boundary_measure', I3_measurableSet

children.name: tile_existence
children.statement: @[implicit_reducible] def tile_existence : TileStructure Q D κ S o where
children.closed_by: each TileStructure field taken from Construction.Ω, Construction.Ω_biUnion, Construction.Ω_disjoint, Construction.Ω_RFD, Construction.ball_subset_Ω₁, Construction.Ω_subset_cball

children.name: tile_sum_operator
children.statement: theorem tile_sum_operator {G' : Set X} {f : X → ℂ} {x : X} (hx : x ∈ G \ G') : ∑ (p : 𝔓 X), carlesonOn p f x = ∑ s ∈ Icc (σ₁ x) (σ₂ x), ∫ y, Ks s x y * f y * exp (I * (Q x y - Q x x))
children.closed_by: the private lemmas 𝔓_biUnion, sum_eq_zero_of_notMem_Icc, 𝔰_eq, exists_Grid, plus the TileStructure fields biUnion_Ω and disjoint_Ω

applicability.goal_shape: A headline theorem ∃ G', MeasurableSet G' ∧ … ≤ C over a concrete metric space X whose conclusion bounds a concrete operator (a per-scale tile sum over Ks and Q), where the same bound has been proved abstractly over a typeclass [TileStructure Q D κ S o] in terms of the abstract operator carlesonSum.
applicability.use_when: A general statement over a typeclass or weaker structure is already proved (discrete_carleson); the concrete setting supplies instances of that structure (grid_existence, tile_existence); and the abstract notion (carlesonSum) rewrites into the concrete one by a named lemma (tile_sum_operator) up to a removable unit-norm phase factor.
applicability.avoid_when: No general theorem exists yet (then instantiation is re-proving, not reuse); the concrete-to-abstract rewrite is itself a deep proof rather than a routine unfold (tile_sum_operator is a 26-line lemma, not a simp lemma); or the concrete statement differs from the abstract one by more than a definitional rewrite plus a unit phase.

consequences: The move shifts all the work out of the concrete theorem: the two structure instantiations (grid_existence, tile_existence) are large field-by-field constructions, and the abstract theorem discrete_carleson is itself proved by a calc chain that bottoms out in the forest estimates forest_union/forest_complement. The glue is nearly definitional — its only non-routine step is removing the constant phase factor exp(-I·Q x x), whose ‖·‖ₑ is shown to be 1 by the suffices at line 123. Failure mode: if the concrete target's operator differs from carlesonSum by more than unfolding plus a unit-norm phase, the simp_rw at line 120 will not close and the abstract theorem must be re-generalised (or a new rewrite lemma proved).
